A.name: 撕纸拼贴 / 干刷版画
A.material: flat torn-paper shapes with dry ink
rules: Rebuild the scene as broad, flat paper shapes, using the permitted simplifications to merge fine detail.
Use uneven fibrous boundaries, restrained dry-brush gaps, and exposed paper within a coherent shallow print surface.
Let the larger shapes and empty paper carry the composition; retain the distinctive protected silhouettes.

B.name: 颗粒拓印 / 流动消散
B.material: sparse rubbing marks and broken ink
rules: Translate the scene into a sparse rubbing with irregular ink deposits and areas of untouched paper.
Keep protected structures readable while secondary boundaries lose ink in the stated flow direction.
Use the palette as restrained print inks; the grain must follow the forms and become sparser toward open paper.

C.name: 平面抽象
C.material: clean opaque shapes on smooth ivory
rules: Reconstruct the visible scene using calm opaque planes and clear relationships between foreground, background, and empty space.
Use smooth ivory as the default surface, with clean flat color boundaries and simplified geometry.
Create abstraction through shape, spacing, overlap, and color, not through simulated material texture.

D.name: 限色丝网印刷
rules: Redraw every part of the scene within one screen-print process using a small shared set of opaque inks.
Use broad ink shapes and deliberate overprint intersections where the source forms overlap.
Allow restrained mesh grain and small imperfect ink boundaries consistently across the image, including formerly photographic areas.
Keep any registration variation subtle enough to preserve all protected structures.

E.name: 通透插画
rules: Redraw the photograph as an airy illustration using translucent color areas and open breathing room between forms.
Use selected crisp structural accents with softer secondary boundaries; make the paper visible through the lighter color areas.
Simplify surface detail into overlapping color washes while keeping the protected geometry and recognizable subject.
avoid: a watercolor filter on a photograph
opaque blocks covering all open space
